issues.description: The reference solution declares toString() with return type Object (public Object toString()) while the exercise and Java's Object.toString() contract expect toString() to return String. The problem statement asks students to implement a custom toString() that returns a descriptive String. The solution's method is annotated with @Override but has the wrong return type, which will cause a compilation error and confuse students about the expected signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's toString() method signature to return String (public String toString()) and ensure it returns the formatted String. Keep the @Override annotation so the method correctly overrides Object.toString(). This aligns the solution with the problem description and Java's expected signature.
